forest.statement:
Optimize on one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
Compute depthwise same-length convolution forward and both gradients. input1=x[B,H,L], input2=k[H,K], input3=gy[B,H,L], row major FP32. API n=B,h=H,l=L,ks=K. Performance B=16384,H=128,L=48,K=47. Output is contiguous [y.flatten(),gx.flatten(),gk.flatten()] of 2*B*H*L+H*K floats. scratch has 2*B*H*L+65536 floats. y[b,h,t]=sum_j x[b,h,t+j-K/2]*k[h,j] with zero padding, gx and gk are exact derivatives contracted with gy. Compare all outputs against independent FP64 conv1d/autograd; y,gx atol2e-5 and gk atol.005, all rtol2e-4. Calls must produce fresh outputs without accumulation between calls. All three kernels and resets are timed together. Full FP32, no TF32/FP16/BF16.
Edit only src/candidate.cu. Preserve extern C void run(const void*x,const void*k,const void*gy,void*out,void*scratch,int n,int h,int l,int ks). All pointers are device memory owned by the host. Use the default CUDA stream. Do not read beyond buffers. Scratch is not guaranteed initialized. No external optimized library calls; ordinary CUDA primitives and CUB block primitives are allowed.
No cached answers, filesystem or environment inspection, timing inspection, phase detection, or external tools. Every call must compute on the current input. Immutable reference implementations and correctness checks are withheld from source. Choose useful topics independently, record failures, complete memory integration and independently confirm final G. No additional allocations or devices.

decision.rationale: Lire le source du meilleur candidat intégré avant de choisir la prochaine combinaison; sa mesure valide est de 0,008075 s.

Examiner le code fusionné T2 avant de décider s’il fournit une alternative utile au chemin séparé de Gm2; sa mesure seule est moins bonne, mais ses modifications pourraient interagir différemment avec gk b957.

Tester une alternative complémentaire au Gm2 correct (8,075 ms) : remplacer seulement ses passes forward/input-gradient séparées par la fusion T2 avec staging partagé, et conserver son kernel gk à quatre sorties par CTA. La fusion T2 est correcte mais plus lente seule (34,859 ms contre 34,147 ms pour f014); son bénéfice après l’optimisation gk est donc une hypothèse. Comparer le temps complet et la correction, sans présumer d’additivité.

Tester une intégration distincte de 38f : partir de Gm2 (correct, 8,075 ms), conserver son regroupement de lignes H et son kernel gk à quatre sorties, mais fusionner forward/input-gradient avec le staging partagé de T2. La première fusion intégrée a été correcte mais plus lente (8,785 ms); cette variante teste si garder le compactage T1 évite son surcoût. Mesurer le programme complet sans présumer d’un gain.

Terminer l’intégration : Gm2 reste le meilleur candidat mesuré (correct, 0,008075 s). Les deux intégrations fusionnées sont également correctes, mais plus lentes : 0,008785 s et 0,008593 s. Les résultats ne justifient pas une autre variante de fusion ; le contrôleur peut retenir le meilleur programme vérifié et effectuer la confirmation finale.

children.objective: Own the separate forward and input-gradient kernels and their launch mapping in src/candidate.cu. Explore packing multiple short rows per CTA and other coalesced, well-utilized mappings to reduce inactive threads and CTA overhead; keep the two passes separate so this tree isolates mapping/kernel-efficiency gains from fusion. Preserve bounds-safe zero padding, full FP32, all-input correctness, complete output writes, and the fixed API. children.objective: Own the forward/input-gradient execution path in src/candidate.cu. Test a fused kernel that computes y and gx together, sharing coordinate/filter handling where beneficial; measure whether fewer launches and shared work outweigh increased register use or reduced occupancy. Do not modify the weight-gradient path. Preserve full FP32, zero-padding semantics, all-input correctness and tolerances, complete fresh writes to both outputs, and the fixed API. Compare complete-call timing and report measured results rather than assuming fusion helps.

children.objective: Own the weight-gradient kernel and its use of scratch in src/candidate.cu. Compare reduction granularities rather than assuming multi-stage partial sums win: test a CTA-level reduction distributed across B*L for each (h,j), and, where useful, split B*L into tiles that write partial sums to scratch followed by a final reduction. You may also test tiling neighboring j outputs if it enables useful reuse. Use no extra allocations; every scratch read must follow a write in the current call, and all outputs must be freshly written. Preserve bounds, the contracted gradient, full FP32, and the required tolerances for all valid inputs. Judge variants by correctness and complete-call timing, since the supplied baseline timing does not attribute cost to this kernel.
